summary: The manuscript reports a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (N=600 task pairs) comparing single‑shot LLM generation and a generate→validate→repair pipeline for intent→vendor‑configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. All 600 shared initial candidates passed a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), so no repairs were invoked; the paired difference is 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0], exact McNemar p=1.0). The paper documents preregistration, archives artifacts (including the required master prompt locator and SHA‑256), and interprets the null outcome as a ceiling effect caused by validator permissiveness and by the shared_initial_candidate design. The study is reproducible from archived artifacts but requires a small set of manuscript clarifications and bibliographic edits before finalisation.
critical_issues: References section is not presented as a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full, consistently formatted metadata for each cited record. Several reference entries are identifier‑only or include ambiguous venue text (e.g., "Comput. Linguistics (or equivalent)"). The manuscript must replace the current reference list with a standard IEEE numbered bibliography using the verified bibliographic metadata archived in the evidence bundle.

Although the manuscript documents shared_initial_candidate semantics, the Abstract and some Introduction phrasing could be read as implying the study measured independent generator‑level differences rather than validator/repair trigger effectiveness. The manuscript must make the estimand–design mapping explicit and unambiguous in the Abstract and in the final paragraph(s) of the Introduction (i.e., state plainly that under shared_initial_candidate semantics the experiment measures validator/repair trigger efficacy, not independent per‑condition generation differences).

A preregistered analysis (seeded 100‑case validator audit) was not executed. While the manuscript notes this in Limitations, the preregistered but unexecuted analysis must be reported prominently in Methods and/or Results with an explicit statement that the confirmatory inference is thus limited and which preregistered inferences remain uncomputed. (This disclosure is required by the preregistration‑fidelity rules.)
required_revisions: Convert the References section into a standard IEEE numbered bibliography. Use the archived terminal_bibliographic_records and other verified metadata to supply full author lists, titles, venue, year, and DOI/URL for each cited work. Ensure every in‑text citation uses IEEE numeric markers that match the reference list.

Edit the Abstract and the final paragraph of the Introduction to state explicitly and unambiguously that the executed contrast used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per pair reused by both arms) and therefore the primary estimand measures validator/repair trigger effectiveness rather than independent generator differences. Remove or reword any sentences that could be interpreted as measuring generation‑level effects.

Prominently report in Methods and/or Results that the preregistered seeded 100‑case validator audit was not executed, and explicitly limit the scope of confirmatory claims accordingly. State which preregistered confirmatory inferences remain uncomputed and how that omission affects interpretation.

Condense the Disclosure Statement to a concise, nonredundant form that preserves all mandatory items (including the single required master_prompt.txt locator and its SHA‑256) but avoids replicating execution‑log level detail already archived. Keep the Disclosure within pages 1–5.

Replace any ambiguous venue metadata in citations (e.g., 'Comput. Linguistics (or equivalent)') with the verified venue or repository name from the archived bibliographic records; if venue metadata is genuinely unavailable for a cited item (e.g., unpublished reports), label it clearly (e.g., 'arXiv preprint') and provide complete author/title/year metadata.
optional_revisions: Add a brief appendix or short paragraph (within the five‑page limit) summarizing a small validator sensitivity check drawn from archived artifacts (for example, the planned but unexecuted 100‑case audit if any partial audits exist) or clearly state that no such audit artifacts exist in the archive.

Expand the Discussion with a concise table mapping possible generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent per‑condition draws) to the estimand each semantics identifies, to help readers design future studies.

If space permits, include a single illustrative example (one paired task) showing the shared_initial_candidate reuse across baseline and guarded episodes with the exact validator trace excerpt (shortened) to aid reader understanding; otherwise reference the archived trace file and its hash in the Disclosure.
